regions.region: title, abstract, and graphical abstract at page top
regions.finding: The title and DOI identify the current article. The graphical abstract is a retrosynthetic/summary depiction connecting ansalactam A, fragment 7, formamide 10, and allene 23; it is not counted as an additional experiment.
Figure 1 shows structures of ansalactams A-D and the prose introduces the synthetic problem; no current-paper reaction conditions or independent experimental arrows occur here.

unresolved: The graphical abstract contains dense stereostructures but is only a summary/retrosynthetic depiction; its structures are not treated as additional experimental records.

regions.finding: Figure 2a is Trauner's cited biomimetic radical-cyclization logic and Figure 2b is the authors' retrosynthetic proposal. These conceptual/cited arrows are not counted as current experimental syntheses.

Six current synthesis sequences were transcribed independently: 12→13 (99%, two operations), 13→14 (84%), 14→15 (99%, two operations), 15→11 (80%), 11→16 (60%, three operations), and 16→10 (75%). Explicit arrow reagents and aqueous carriers were structured; temperatures, times, charges, workup, purification, and yield bases remain unreported.

The prose supports the 10→17→18 and 10+9→19→20 sequences shown on page 3, including 18 as a single isolated diastereomer with X-ray assignment, the 28% overall yield to 20 over two steps, one isolated regioisomer with uncertain overall selectivity, and X-ray-supported rearrangement of 20.

Actual mechanistic observations (isolation/X-ray confirmation of 21 and its competence in the [3+2] reaction) were separated from the proposed 22/21 pathway. Neutral/basic no-reaction controls and failed functionalization of 18 lack discrete conditions and remain source context rather than fabricated experiments.

unresolved: No SI was supplied, so the main-paper summaries do not establish complete experimental procedures or measurement bases.
Individual conditions for failed functionalization of 18 and neutral/basic controls are not specified.
The operative intermediate (protonated isocyanide 22 versus protonated oxazole 21) remains explicitly unresolved by the authors.

regions.finding: Four independent experimental arrows were recorded: formal [3+2] reactions 10+methyl acrylate→17 (65%) and 10+9→19 (49%), followed by mCPBA oxidations 17→18 (90%, single diastereomer) and 19→20 (57%). The prose-supported 28% two-step yield to 20 is retained separately from the 57% second-arrow yield.

Figure 3a is an initially envisioned reactivity model. Figure 3b combines the proposed 22/21 pathway with the actual isolation of 21 and its demonstrated reaction competence; conceptual and experimental content were stored separately.

All six table entries were made independent optimization records. Each retains the common Tf2O (1.1 equiv)/CH2Cl2/0 °C/45 min preactivation and its own wet Et3N loading, allene 23 loading, subsequent solvent, rt duration, concentration, and 24 result. Footnotes establish wet Et3N in every row and isolated E/Z-isomer yield after column chromatography. Entry 2 preserves CH2Cl2 for preactivation and toluene for the later stage rather than collapsing them.

The two arrows 24→25 (H2, Pd/C, EtOH) and 25→7 (Pinnick oxidation) form one explicitly reported two-step sequence. The 63% value is scoped from 24 to 7 over two steps, not assigned to the second arrow alone; 7 is reported as a single isolated diastereomer.

unresolved: Exact E/Z and diastereomer ratios for 24 are not reported.
The concentration basis and reaction scale for Figure 4a are not stated in the main paper.
Figure 4b does not provide times, temperatures, pressure, quantities, Pinnick reagent composition, workup/purification, or yield/selectivity measurement bases.
Dense structures 17-25 and 7 are not assigned speculative machine SMILES where exact stereochemical encoding was unsafe.
